land.text: Vaspurakan, the Artsruni lands round Lake Van, held until 908 under Abbasid suzerainty: Khatchik-Gagik II Artsruni 'was the first of the Artsrunis to rule Vaspurakan under Abbasid suzerainty'

predecessors.note: The Artsruni were Abbasid vassals before 908; the Abbasid caliph (or, in the body of the Kingdom of Vaspurakan page, the Sajid emir Yusuf) recognised Gagik as king in 908. The bagratid-armenia dossier (eu-19-b) records the same year as the land leaving the Bagratid kingdom; both slugs are given as counterparts.

land.text: Vaspurakan, inside Cliopatria's Bagratid Armenia shapes of 886-910 until the Artsruni kingdom was recognised in 908

predecessors.note: Added by reviewer eu-19-d (2026-10-31) so that the note above holds: Cliopatria's bagratid-armenia shapes 886..898 (to 910) cover the Van basin, and the bagratid-armenia dossier records a 908 loss to kingdom-of-vaspurakan; the Kingdom of Vaspurakan page has Gagik 'recognized as king by the Sajid ruler Yusuf' and allied with him 'to attack the Bagratuni kingdom'.

land.text: the whole kingdom: 'the Kingdom of Vaspurakan became the Byzantine theme of Vasprakania'

successors.note: Senekerim-Hovhannes received Sebasteia, Evdokia and possibly Amasia in exchange and settled there with 14,000 retainers; the Byzantine theme lasted until 1071 on the Artsruni dynasty page.

capitals.name: Van
capitals.note: The infobox says 'Capital: Van' but the body says 'The Kingdom of Vaspurakan had no specific capital'; court seats named are Van, Ostan/Vostan (modern Gevas) and the island of Aghtamar in Lake Van.

rulers.name: Derenik-Ashot
rulers.note: Infobox '937/943-958/959'; the body gives 'King (943-953)' and says he 'died without an heir in 953'.

rulers.name: Gurgen-Khachik
rulers.note: Infobox '991-1003', overlapping Ashot-Sahak; the page elsewhere has his son Derenik 'lord of Antzivazik by 1004'.

rulers.name: Seneqerim-Hovhannes
rulers.note: Infobox '1003-1021'; ceded the kingdom to Byzantium in 1021.

correction.text: the first Cliopatria shape drawn three years early: Gagik I 'recognized as King of Armenia by Arab Caliph: 908', Vaspurakan comprising 'the lands between Lake Van and Lake Urmia in 908'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the kingdom in 911; the infobox founding is 908. The 911 shape is reused unchanged, because no page opened gives a different extent for 908-910.

41,513 km2 against 'Vaspurakan's territory was 40,870 km2 (16,000 sq mi) and was divided into 35 cantons' (the Vaspurakan region page, no year): ratio 1.02. The bbox (42.07-45.37 E) fits 'the lands between Lake Van and Lake Urmia'. The Kingdom page adds that the Artsruni 'temporarily in the 910s, controlled parts of the provinces of Ayrarat, Taron and Korchayk'; those parts are outside this shape and the page does not date them, so no event is written.
41,636 km2; the +0.3% change from 911-935 is cell-level noise, no page dates a gain or loss at 936. Gagik I's death in 943 and the succession of Derenik-Ashot are dynastic, not territorial.

41,810 km2, the maximum; again a sub-1% change that no page explains. Derenik-Ashot 'died without an heir in 953' on the Kingdom page but the infobox gives his reign to 958/959; the extent is not discussed.
41,636 km2; no territorial event on the page for the 980s. Unverified beyond the area: page budget.

40,952 km2 (-1.6%). The infobox has Gurgen-Khachik ruling from 991 and his son Derenik 'lord of Antzivazik by 1004', which hints at a cadet principality at Antzevatsik/Andzevatsik carved from the kingdom; the page does not say where or what share, so the shape stands. The 1016 Seljuk raid 'devastated' the kingdom without a recorded border change.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but only to 1021: 'In 1021, he also secured the cession of the Kingdom of Vaspurakan by its king Seneqerim-John'; from December 1021 the land is Byzantine, so the shape must not run to 1027

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws the kingdom to 1027, six years after the cession (Basil II page: 1021; Artsruni dynasty page: 'the Kingdom of Vaspurakan became the Byzantine theme of Vasprakania, which lasted for fifty years until 1071'). The Byzantine Empire row (eu-05) must carry the land from 1022.

region.text: 'Gagik I recognized as King of Armenia by Arab Caliph: 908'; 'At its greatest extent Vaspurakan comprised the lands between Lake Van and Lake Urmia in 908'

ledger.note: 908: Gagik Artsruni is recognised as king and Vaspurakan stands as a kingdom between Lake Van and Lake Urmia. The infobox credits an Arab caliph and the body 'the Sajid ruler Yusuf' (Sajid page: a caliphate army was sent against Yusuf in 908); the Sajid emir Afshin had 'occupied' Vaspurakan in 900. The page names the lakes, not a frontier, so the region is the Cliopatria 911 shape.

region.text: the whole kingdom, ceded to Basil II

ledger.note: 1021: King Senekerim-Hovhannes gives Vaspurakan to the Byzantine Empire. Basil II page: 'In 1021, he also secured the cession of the Kingdom of Vaspurakan by its king Seneqerim-John'; 'In December, George's ally the Armenian king Senekerim of Vaspurakan, who was being harassed by the Seljuk Turks, surrendered his kingdom to the emperor'. The Kingdom of Vaspurakan page adds the exchange: Sebasteia and its territories to the Euphrates; the land becomes the theme of Vasprakania (or Media). Cliopatria keeps the kingdom to 1027.

wars.name: Artsruni-Sajid alliance against the Bagratid kingdom
wars.outcome: No border result recorded: 'Gagik I Artsruni was recognized as king by the Sajid ruler Yusuf and allied with the latter to attack the Bagratuni kingdom'; after Smbat's death at Yusuf's hands in 914 'Gagik allied with the new Bagratuni king Ashot II'.
wars.note: Years 908 and 914 are the pages' own; the campaigns are undated and no ground changed hands on any page opened. The Sajid page gives only that 'Much of the Sajids' energies were spent in attempting to take control of neighboring Armenia' and that Yusuf's frontier ran to Ani and Dabil (Dvin).

wars.name: Seljuk raid on Vaspurakan
wars.outcome: 'In 1016, the kingdom was devastated by a raid by the Seljuq Turks'; no land changed hands, but harassment by the Seljuk Turks is the Basil II page's reason for the 1021 surrender.
wars.note: The raiders are the Turkmen forerunners of the Seljuks, not the Great Seljuk state (founded later); great-seljuk-empire is the nearest dossier.

certainty.note: A highland kingdom described by lakes and 35 cantons; no treaty or survey line is on any page. The line with the Byzantine Empire was a cession of the whole kingdom, not a boundary.

sources.title: Kingdom of Vaspurakan
sources.note: Identity, founding 908, rulers, extent, 1016 raid, 1021 cession, theme of Vasprakania.

sources.title: Artsruni dynasty
sources.note: 908 investiture under Abbasid suzerainty; 1021 exchange for Sebaste, Evdokia and possibly Amasia; theme to 1071. Thin on the Sajids and on dates between 908 and 1021.

sources.title: Sajid dynasty
sources.note: Context: Yusuf's tribute and frontier (908-914). Does not mention Vaspurakan or the Artsruni.

sources.title: Vaspurakan
sources.note: Area 40,870 km2 in 35 cantons (the sanity check on Cliopatria's 41.5 k km2).

sources.title: Basil II
sources.note: 1021 cession and its December date; the Georgian campaign of 1021-1022 that surrounds it.

notes: Cliopatria's six shapes (911-1027) are one near-constant outline of about 41,000 km2, which agrees with the Vaspurakan region page (40,870 km2). Two corrections: the kingdom starts in 908, three years before the first shape, and ends in December 1021, six years before the last. The shape changes at 936, 947, 980 and 990 are under 2% and no page explains them. Ledger is deliberately short: the pages date no gain or loss between 908 and 1021. Page silent: the 'temporary' hold of parts of Ayrarat, Taron and Korchayk 'in the 910s' (Kingdom of Vaspurakan page) has no year; the bagratid-armenia dossier dates the Nakhchavan hand-over to Ashot Artsruni to 902 and its return to 904, which no page opened here confirms. The Artsruni cadet branch of Antzivazik (Gurgen-Khachik, 991-1003) may be a separate lordship; page silent on its land. Pages used: 5 of 5. Region names the gazetteer lacks: 'Vaspurakan' (use the admin-1 Van plus Hakkari and the shores of Lake Van and Lake Urmia, Cliopatria's shape is the stand-in), 'Antzevatsik' (Andzevatsik, near Van). Counterparts: abbasid-caliphate (me-08), bagratid-armenia (eu-19), sajid-dynasty (me-08), byzantine-empire (eu-05) all have rows; the Byzantine Empire row needs the land from 1022 and the Bagratid row records the 908 loss.
